name: BrokenFreezerSister
source:
`` **Fuck! **'' I shouted. Slamming the door of my apartment behind me as I walked in, digging my nails as I gripped a necklace. 
 
 `` *The fuck's got you in a knot? *'' My roommate shouted from the other room. 
 
 I ignored her, walking into the kitchen and opening the fridge. Grabbing a jug of milk and a glass, I poured myself a drink. Opening the freezer, I found a tupperware that was supposed to have the remains of an ice-cream cake, and cracking it open, I found it melted. Even the Oreos were soggy. Great. The freezer lost power. I threw it in the garbage, tupperware and all. 
 
 `` **Fuck! **'' I shouted. 
 
 My roommate, Elise, stormed in. `` *What is it?! *'' She shouted. 
 
 `` **Nothing! I just... I come home from... The fucking freezer is shot, and this is JUST what I fucking needed after -- Fuck! **'' 
 
 `` *Oh my god, man! *'' Elise slapped me. `` *Get it together! *'' 
 
 I stopped. Took several deep breaths. Sat down with my milk and put my head on the counter. 
 
 `` *What happened? You did n't say where you were going. *'' 
 
 `` **I was visiting my little sister. **'' 
 
 `` *Oh. That's nice of you. *'' 
 
 I looked down at a necklace, still clutched in my fingers. It was a dogtag, one of two. Engraved in the one resting on my palm was a name. 
 
 *Brianna. * 
 
 `` **Nice does n't save lives. **''
retelling:
From the perspective of Elise, roommate and concerned friend:

In the heart of an ordinary apartment, tucked away in a bustling city, lived two young women - myself and my roommate, who I would soon come to know as the troubled narrator. Our shared abode, though modest, was more than just a roof over our heads; it was a sanctuary where we sought solace and comfort at the end of each day.

On this particular day, the usual tranquility of our home was shattered by an unusual commotion as I heard the front door slam shut with a force that resonated through the hallway. My instincts told me something was amiss, so I walked out to check on the narrator.

As I entered their room, I found them standing in the kitchen, visibly agitated and gripping tightly onto an object dangling from a silver chain - a dog tag engraved with the name "Brianna." The sight of it sent a chill down my spine, as I knew all too well that this was no ordinary trinket for the narrator.

Curiosity piqued, I decided to approach them cautiously. With a gentle voice and a concerned expression, I asked what had happened. To my surprise, they revealed that they had just returned from visiting their little sister. However, their distress didn't stem merely from a broken freezer or a long journey home; it was rooted in a deeper pain, one that I could sense but not yet fully understand.

I knew Brianna - the name etched onto that dog tag - as well, having met her during our childhood visits to the narrator's family home. She was lively and spirited, always quick with a smile and a story to share. The thought of anything happening to her weighed heavy on my heart.

In that moment, I felt a surge of empathy for my roommate, as they struggled to find words to express their feelings. I could sense the turmoil boiling beneath the surface, threatening to overflow at any second. As a friend, it was my duty to support them through this difficult time and help them seek the answers they so desperately needed.

In retrospect, that day marked the beginning of a new chapter in our lives - one filled with uncertainty, but also hope for healing and understanding. Together, we would navigate the stormy waters of the narrator's emotional distress, holding onto the memories of Brianna as our guiding light.
